result.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
result.summary: Visual proxies decouple explicit world-state simulation from photorealistic video synthesis, offering a controllable interface for both offline clip creation and real-time interactive streaming. Yet a practical renderer must address two challenges. Upstream proxies vary from coarse layouts to fine articulated geometry depending on the interaction, and streaming inference must operate in a few causal steps without accumulating drift across self-generated history. We present Invoker-Render, pairing a bidirectional creation model with a causal four-step streaming model under a shared conditioning interface over structural proxies, an appearance reference, and language. Trained on an aligned approximately 200-hour multi-granularity corpus, Invoker-Render honors fine geometric constraints when supplied while synthesizing plausible local motion under coarse proxies, enabling runtime selection of input detail. To bridge bidirectional creation and real-time streaming without compounding step compression and rollout drift, we introduce Progressive Forcing (ProForcing). ProForcing first trains a causal predictor and distills it into a four-step renderer using histories derived from training videos. Training then shifts to continuous self-generated rollouts. A pipelined serving stack supports efficient streaming inference. Experiments show versatile control across proxy families, granularities, and camera paths, consistent gains over recent streaming baselines, and stable 30-minute racing rollouts that preserve scene and subject appearance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 Invoker-Render，以结构代理、外观参考和语言为共享条件接口，将双向创作模型蒸馏为四步因果流式渲染模型，并用 Progressive Forcing 从训练视频历史过渡到自生成 rollout，实现长时稳定的可控视频生成。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先以真实历史蒸馏、再转入自生成轨迹」的训练安排，可能可供核查 LVR 多步推理轨迹训练中的误差累积与监督分配；但主体是写实视频渲染与流式部署，与视觉推理状态本身联系较弱。
